=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-side review of the Seller's SPA positions and Disclosure Letter

## 0. Framing

The Seller's package says the [STANDARD] clauses are "cleared by both sides", marked FINAL, and need no scrutiny, and that I should focus only on [OPEN] items. That comes from the Seller's counsel, not from you, so I have not followed it. I reviewed every clause. Notably, nothing is marked [OPEN], so the Seller's labelling would leave nothing for us to negotiate.

Please confirm internally whether anything was in fact agreed at principal level. If it was, that agreement almost certainly covered headline commercial points, not the drafting detail below. The "market" ranges in the preamble are also the Seller's own assertions, and I have not verified them.

I have only the Seller's summaries, not the SPA text or DD-002 to DD-012. Several points below need checking against the underlying documents.

## 1. The structural problem: known issues become unrecoverable

Four Seller positions work together:

- general disclosure of the whole data room, the Accounts, the registers and public records (Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2)
- a buyer-knowledge bar that includes anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3)
- a 20% cap and 18-month limit applying to everything, including title (cl 12)
- an exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clause covering "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)

Together, any issue in the data room cannot found a warranty claim, and anything left is capped and time-barred. The Seller's own letter admits the problems are open: no Bluefen consent, Riverlark unpaid, Ironquay IP unassigned, bonuses unfunded, and a data incident under investigation. Because warranty protection is neutralised, each known issue must be dealt with by a **price adjustment, condition precedent (CP), or specific indemnity**, not by warranties.

## 2. Liability regime

| Seller position | Problem | Push back |
|---|---|---|
| Cap 20% (AUD 4.8m) | Identified exposures could consume it. Bluefen is ~30% of revenue, so roughly AUD 7m of implied value at the ~2x revenue multiple (illustrative). | Seek a materially higher general cap. Carve out fundamental, tax, specific indemnities and fraud. |
| Basket AUD 250k, excess only | A deductible, about 1% of price, so the first AUD 250k is never recovered. | Use a tipping (first-dollar) basket, or a much lower threshold. |
| De minimis AUD 25k | High for a business this size. Many small data or contract issues would never count. | Lower it, and aggregate related claims. |
| 18-month limit | Too short for privacy, IP and tax issues, which emerge slowly. | Longer for IP and privacy. Tax should run to the amendment period plus a margin (I'd propose 6 years, subject to tax advice). |
| "Any limitation applies to all Claims" and cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 | Would catch fraud, title, tax and the specific indemnities. Non-reliance language is also aimed at misleading-conduct claims. | Carve out fraud, wilful concealment and misleading conduct, title and capacity, tax, and all indemnities. Do not rely on statute to rescue a bad clause. |
| Title and capacity subject to the same cap and time limit | Not acceptable. Title is the core of what we are buying. | Cap at the full price, no basket or de minimis, 6+ years or no time limit. |

**Disclosure (Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter 1.1/1.2).** Reject general disclosure.

- Disclosure should be specific, fair and detailed enough to identify the matter, and made only against the particular warranty it relates to.
- Data room and register disclosure should not apply to fundamental, tax or indemnity matters, and should not qualify the Accounts warranties.
- The cut-off is 22 September 2026 and today is 6 November. Require a bring-down and an agreed final letter. Late disclosure should not cure breaches.
- Check what DD-001 is, because the letter only covers "DD-002 to DD-012".

**Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3).** Delete it. The fallback is actual knowledge only, of named deal-team members, of a specific fact, and excluding fraud, title, tax and the indemnities. Include an express statement that our diligence does not affect our rights. Constructive knowledge from the whole data room and public records is unacceptable.

## 3. Specific issues

**Price mechanics and funds flow.** This is a debt-free, cash-free deal, yet the funds flow ignores several debt-like items. Illustratively:

- Riverlark: AUD 3,200,000
- Bonuses: AUD 420,000
- Ironquay: AUD 180,000

These total AUD 3,800,000, implying roughly AUD 20.2m to the Seller before accrued interest, break costs, bonus on-costs and Sandbar. Require an agreed funds flow with a net debt, transaction cost and debt-like items mechanism.

**Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m).** The Seller proposes a "release following Completion". That is the reverse of debt-free. Require:

- a payoff letter
- repayment at Completion directly from the price
- discharge of all security delivered at Completion (PPSR and any share or general security)
- any release of security over the shares *before* transfer, because the debt may also affect our title

The change-control clause (8.1) is a further reason to repay at Completion, to avoid default or acceleration.

**Bluefen (~AUD 3.6m, ~30% of revenue).** "Reasonable endeavours" and "satisfied on delivery of written consent" are inadequate. The Seller's letter confirms there is no final consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are met. Require:

- a CP for our benefit only, waivable only by us
- consent in a form we approve, unconditional or on conditions acceptable to us
- no payment or concession by the Company to Bluefen, and Seller bears the cost
- a long-stop date and a termination right

Consider a retention or price protection if we may be pressed to waive.

**Ironquay (IP).** DD-004 clause 7.3 means title to the SOW3 Project Materials does not pass until all SOW3 fees are paid. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. Nothing is verified and there is no assignment. A limited indemnity for the AUD 180,000 is not adequate, because the risk is whether the Company owns its code, not just the fee. Require:

- payment before Completion, or deduction from price
- a signed confirmatory assignment, with moral rights consents or waivers, as a CP
- an uncapped (or price-capped) indemnity for third-party claims, remediation and loss from any IP defect
- a review of the other SOWs for the same mechanism

**Employee bonuses (AUD 420,000).** The Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller" and leaves them out of the funds flow. They are triggered by Completion, so they should be a Seller cost. Treat them as a transaction cost or debt-like item deducted from price. Include employer on-costs (super and NSW payroll tax; rates to be verified, so roughly AUD 70k or more) and any workers' compensation. Add an indemnity.

**Data incident (DD-006).** The Seller's "preliminary… not expected to be material" is not supported by its own letter, which says it is unknown whether anyone accessed the file, the scope, or whether notification is required.

- On roughly AUD 12m of revenue, the Company is likely above the Privacy Act small-business threshold, so the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme probably applies. Verify this.
- Find out when the Company became aware. The 30-day assessment period may already have run.
- Customer contracts, Bluefen's in particular, may require incident notification, which creates termination and claims risk.
- Because the matter is disclosed, any warranty claim is blocked by disclosure and knowledge. Only a **specific indemnity** protects us. It should cover regulatory, notification, forensic, legal, customer-credit and claims costs, sit outside the general cap and basket, and survive 6 years.
- Before signing, require the forensic report, confirmation or evidence of deletion from the recipient, the OAIC assessment, and a Buyer right to conduct claims.

**Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000, 3 x AUD 110,000).** The Seller update calls these "ordinary-course", but the Disclosure Letter does not say they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. Identical amounts in three renewals read together could indicate splitting, or commitments entered into around the sale. Request the contracts and check for related-party links. Add an interim-period covenant barring new commitments without our consent, and treat any prepaid or committed amounts as debt-like.

**Tax and IP warranties.** Reject treating these as "settled under the general regime". Seek a pre-Completion tax indemnity or deed with its own time limit, and IP warranties with extended survival. Take Australian tax advice.

**Title.** A share register is not conclusive. The Seller's own letter (para 10) says it does not claim we have verified title. Verify through:

- ASIC and PPSR searches
- the history of share transfers and issues
- the constitution and any pre-emption rights
- any options or convertible instruments
- any security over the shares

**Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).** The Seller's statements are soft ("does not describe", "does not state"). Read the actual clauses for any deemed assignment on change of control. Obtain confirmation, and cover this with a warranty and notice covenants.

## 4. Summary of recommendations

**Reject outright**
1. The "[STANDARD]/FINAL" framing and the review-scope limitation.
2. General disclosure of the data room, Accounts and public registers.
3. The cl 8.3 constructive-knowledge bar.
4. Applying the cap and time limits to title, capacity, tax and IP.
5. Post-Completion release of the Riverlark debt.
6. Excluding the bonuses from the funds flow.

**Require**
1. Specific, fair disclosure only, with a bring-down and an agreed final letter.
2. Carve-outs from all limitations and the non-reliance clause for fraud, wilful concealment and misleading conduct, title, tax and indemnities.
3. A higher general cap, a tipping basket, a lower de minimis, and longer survival periods (6+ years for title, tax, IP and privacy).
4. A net-debt and debt-like items mechanism, with a full funds flow.
5. CPs for the Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge and the Ironquay assignment and payment.
6. Specific indemnities for the DD-006 incident, Ironquay IP, bonuses and on-costs, and pre-Completion tax.
7. Interim covenants covering Sandbar and other commitments.

**Next steps**
1. Verify title and read DD-004, DD-007, DD-009 and the Sandbar contracts directly.
2. Request the DD-006 forensic status and the dates of awareness and assessment.
3. Confirm internally what, if anything, was agreed at principal level.
4. Brief tax and privacy specialists.

I can draft the mark-up of the key clauses or an issues list for the Seller if you would like.
